evidence_detail: 4 obs / 4 DOIs in the +/-0.5 K cluster: T=298.0 eps=17.6 (10.1016/j.fluid.2013.12.014, MSR-29e3026c33ebc6a8, P=101 kPa, f=0); T=298.15 eps=16.58 (10.1021/je900503p, MSR-644e137ed8fac806, P=101); T=298.15 eps=16.6 (10.1021/je3007666, MSR-790ead4efdd5221b, P=100); T=298.15 eps=16.6 (10.1021/je800593p, MSR-8f17666d0a81b3c0, P=101). min=16.58 max=17.6; spread=(17.6-16.58)/16.58=6.152% -> register's 6.15% CONFIRMED. TEMPERATURE: intra-cluster dT=298.15-298.0=0.15 K only. At the task's -0.25 %/K that is 0.0375% of eps = 0.61% of the 6.15% spread. At the molecule's OWN measured slope (-0.1635 eps/K from a 7-point consensus fit, i.e. -0.96 %/K) it is 0.15*0.1635=0.025 eps = 0.15% = 2.4% of the spread. Either way temperature explains <3%, so it CANNOT explain the spread: closing 6.02% would need 6.3 K at the measured slope or 24.1 K at -0.25 %/K, versus 0.15 K actual and a 0.5 K window. V06 PROVENANCE: 16.6 is the exact median of the 10 in-window (293.15-303.15 K) values [15.75,15.75,15.75,16.58,16.6,16.6,17.51,17.51,17.51,17.6] and also the median of the 4 cluster values [16.58,16.6,16.6,17.6]. It is an ACTUALLY OBSERVED value (holders MSR-790ead4efdd5221b and MSR-8f17666d0a81b3c0, both 16.6), not an interpolation. 17.6 sits +6.02% from the median; 16.58 sits -0.12%. OUTLIER DIAGNOSIS: 17.6 is from a DMSO+monohydric-alcohol MIXTURE study (Guo-Zhu & Jie, Fluid Phase Equilib. 2013) whose seven 'pure' endpoints are 49, 33.1, 22.8, 21.3, 19.1, 17.8, 17.6 - a mixture-series endpoint, not a dedicated pure-liquid measurement, and it is the only cluster member measured by microwave network analyser rather than a capacitive/dielectrometer method. Against same-T consensus medians that source is biased in BOTH directions (DMSO +6.36%, butan-2-ol +6.02%, but 2-propanol -8.65%, ethanol -13.83%, methanol -4.33%, 1-butanol -2.68%), mean bias -2.69% with mixed sign, so it is not a uniform calibration offset - it is a low-reliability endpoint source. Its 17.6 is 5.4% off the molecule's own trend and corresponds to 292.5 K, i.e. 5.5 K away from the labelled 298 K. INDEPENDENCE: the 4 DOIs are only 3 author-groups. 10.1021/je3007666 (Klimaszewski, Borun, Bald, Sengwa) and 10.1021/je800593p (Chmielewska, Zurada, Klimaszewski, Bald) share Klimaszewski+Bald and agree on 15/15 shared (mol,T) points to 1e-9 - one measurement lineage counted twice. Effective independent evidence = 3 groups: two agree at 16.58-16.6, one disagrees at 17.6. VERDICT: 16.6 is correct and well supported; the 6.15% is one mixture-paper endpoint against a duplicated consensus, not an unresolved measurement conflict. Keep 16.6. Caveat: the conflict_id anchor is 298.0 rather than 298.15 (see the ALL row) - the label is order-dependent, though the membership and the 6.152% number are stable.

3 obs / 3 DOIs, ALL at exactly T=303.15 K (dT=0.000 K, so temperature contributes nothing at all): eps=37.72 (10.1016/j.fluid.2008.01.024, MSR-5e013323fd6f27cb, P=101 kPa, f=0, capacitive method); eps=37.72 (10.1016/j.fluid.2009.07.009, MSR-de55e6c75a57f2a5, P=101.325, f=0, parallel-plate); eps=38.67 (10.1021/je9002515, MSR-fe12c1254a29e890, P=101, f=0, parallel-plate). min=37.72 max=38.67; spread=(38.67-37.72)/37.72=2.519% -> register's 2.52% CONFIRMED. V06 PROVENANCE: 37.72 is the median of [37.72,37.72,38.67] and an observed value held by two rows. But those two rows are NOT independent: 10.1016/j.fluid.2008.01.024 (Sengwa, Khatri, Sankhla) and 10.1016/j.fluid.2009.07.009 (Sengwa, Sankhla, Khatri) are the same three authors and agree EXACTLY on 5/5 shared (mol,T) points (37.72, 41.17, 17.18, 106.14, 36.55 - all identical to 1e-9). The register's n_distinct_sources=3 is a count of DOI strings, not of independent measurements; author-level independent groups = 2. So the 'median of 3' is really a 1-vs-1 tie, and the median rule breaks that tie arbitrarily in favour of the duplicated pair. SHAPE TEST (favours 38.67): 10.1021/je9002515 (Swiergiel & Jadzyn) reports DMAc at 10 temperatures 303.15-393.15 K as one coherent curve: 38.67, 36.551, 34.678, 32.949, 31.458, 29.954, 28.578, 27.287, 26.074, 24.923. Forcing 303.15 to 37.72 raises the fit RMS from 0.0684 to 0.1332 (1.9x, deg 2) and from 0.0266 to 0.1113 (4.2x, deg 3). Extrapolating the nine 313.15-393.15 K points back to 303.15 K gives 38.375 (deg 2, all 9), 38.638 (deg 2, first 4) and 38.568 (first 3) - all within 0.03-0.30 of 38.67 and 0.66-0.92 away from 37.72; even a straight line gives 37.483, i.e. BELOW 37.72, so 37.72 sits under the linear continuation while 38.67 sits on the curvature. The implied first-interval slope is -0.212 /K if eps(303.15)=38.67, matching the later observed slopes (-0.187, -0.173, -0.149, -0.150; mean -0.165 /K), whereas 37.72 implies an anomalous -0.117 /K that breaks monotone steepening. 38.67 also recurs as the x->0 endpoint of the DMAc + N-methylacetamide mixture series in the same paper (block 5, first prop = 38.67). WHY THIS IS STILL A HOLD, NOT AN ADOPTION: internal coherence establishes the SHAPE of the Swiergiel curve, not its ABSOLUTE accuracy. A self-consistent series can still be uniformly offset, and a single-point source can be correct. The two 37.72 rows also carry a 95% combined uncertainty of 0.23 and the 38.67 row 0.387, and the 0.95 gap exceeds both, so uncertainty does not arbitrate either. Nothing in the ledger decides whether Swiergiel's absolute scale or Sengwa's single point is right. VERDICT: HOLD. v06's 37.72 is not established as correct - it is an artefact of counting one duplicated lineage as two independent sources. The decision needs the primary documents (Swiergiel & Jadzyn calibration/absolute scale, and Sengwa's sample purity and thermostat accuracy). Note that this conflict is currently in the model-ready set, so the HOLD is consequential.

THREE systemic defects, all reproduced by running the scripts. (D1) GREEDY ANCHOR CLUSTERING IS ORDER-DEPENDENT AND CAN SILENTLY DROP A CONFLICT. build_source_conflict_register.py:207-224 builds each temperature cluster as 'anchor row i + every later unused row j with |T_i - T_j| <= 0.5', never re-checking the cluster's own span. Being anchor-radial rather than span/complete-linkage, it can split or merge differently depending on row order. Measured: over 201 random row orders, 24 of 153 molecules yield a DIFFERENT clustering; BTANRVKWQNVYAZ alone shows 117 distinct clusterings and its conflict_id flips between 'MCONF-BTANRVKWQNVYAZ-298.15' (1502/2000 shuffles) and 'MCONF-BTANRVKWQNVYAZ-298' (498/2000) - the anchor, hence the ID, is a coin flip on row order. Minimal reproducer: rows (297.0,20.0), (297.4,20.1), (297.9,25.0) span 0.9 K with every adjacent pair <=0.5 K; order A,B,C and A,C,B return ZERO conflicts (a 24.4% disagreement silently lost), while B,A,C returns one 3-row 25.00% conflict and C,B,A a 2-row 24.38% conflict. This defeats the register's own stated purpose (docstring lines 9-11: conflicts should enter the queue 'by construction rather than by luck'). It does NOT corrupt either adjudicated conflict's numbers: DMAc gives anchor 303.15, the same 3 rows and 2.5186% in 2000/2000 shuffles; butan-2-ol always gives the same 4 rows and 6.152%, only the label flips. Fix: sort by temperature and use a span-based (complete-linkage) cluster, or bucket by (molecule, T rounded to tolerance) with an explicit max-span assertion. (D2) v06 IS BLIND TO THE CONFLICT REGISTER. build_dataset_v06.py never reads measurement_conflict_register.csv or source_conflict_register.csv - the tokens 'conflict', 'MCONF', 'measurement_conflict_register', 'source_conflict_register' all return 0 hits in that file. model_ready is computed at lines 187-199 from pressure/pair/temperature/band only, so resolution_status='UNRESOLVED' is never consulted. Consequence: 2 of 74 model-ready rows (2.70%) carry an unresolved conflict - v04row-010 butan-2-ol (16.6) and v04row-021 DMAc (37.72) - both with flags=NONE and blocking_reasons='' so they look perfectly clean. The other 14 conflicted molecules are excluded only incidentally (they happen to be PRESSURE_HETEROGENEOUS or PAIR_NOT_VALID), and one conflicted molecule (UJPMYEOUBPIPHQ, 5.45%) is ABSENT from v06 entirely. v06's exclusion of conflicts is therefore accidental, not a rule, and the two conflicts that survive are exactly the two under adjudication. (D3) v06 EXCLUSION TALLY IS DOUBLE-COUNTED. build_dataset_v06.py appends 'NO_CONTRIBUTING_MEASUREMENT' at lines 171-173 (excl_reason) and again at lines 196-197 (the 'not members' branch), so 147 of 174 exclusion rows carry that reason TWICE. The manifest's exclusions_by_reason sums to 514 across 174 excluded rows, reporting NO_CONTRIBUTING_MEASUREMENT as 294 when the true distinct-row count is 147. Correct distinct-row counts: PAIR_NOT_VALID 170, NO_CONTRIBUTING_MEASUREMENT 147, TEMPERATURE_IMPUTED 22, PRESSURE_HETEROGENEOUS 15, SYNTHETIC_PAIR 11, OUTSIDE_ROOM_BAND 2 (367 reason-hits over 174 rows). The per-reason histogram in dataset_v06_manifest.json is unusable as a denominator. REPRODUCIBILITY (tested, PASSES): running build_source_conflict_register.py twice gives byte-identical measurement_conflict_register.csv (sha256 a7637bc64b7e7a244cb57d0ed3e949d63ddf9f2be5f03762a684ab5d12fab3de both runs) and source_conflict_register.csv (sha256 395a4c98651f96e40f3d536d84e362abf63fdf7976930098afc7627ad064de6f both runs). Only generated_at_utc in the .json/.md varies, as expected. Determinism therefore holds for the CURRENT row order only; D1 shows it would not survive a re-ordered input. SYSTEMIC VERDICT: FAIL on the machinery (D1/D2/D3), RETAIN_PARALLEL for the two molecules - keep both values visible, never average - until conflict status becomes an explicit model_ready gate.
